summary: One value-preserving tensor-core tile layout read by both the decode GEMV and FP8 / NVFP4 prompt GEMMs, with a k permutation and an intra-quad exchange instead of per-call re-layout
implementation_scope: CUDA repack kernels for row-major FP8 and NVFP4 weights, per-token FP8 and static-scale NVFP4 activation packing, W8A8 (mma m16n8k32 e4m3) and W4A4 (mma m16n8k64 kind::mxf4nvf4 scale_vec::4X) prompt GEMMs with register-ring weights, cp.async activations, two row tiles per warp and fixed-order split-K, repacking straight into concatenated or gate | up interleaved matrices, a gated-MLP epilogue (SiLU, tanh-GELU, erf-GELU) writing BF16 act(gate) * up, host launch planning; a 1-16 row decode / verify GEMV over the same tiles on BF16 tensor cores (sm_80+, software E4M3 / E2M1 decodes where the hardware conversions are missing) with bitwise row invariance, plain and gated, and its block shape derived from N, the SM count and occupancy; W8A16 / W4A16 prompt GEMMs over the same tiles (exact BF16 decode in registers, BF16 mma with ldmatrix activations, FP32 fold every 512 columns, one-wave K split), plain and gated, sm_80+; a device fragment probe; a pure-Python model of tiles, register assembly and both MMAs; checkpoint sources that read an NVFP4 (compressed-tensors or ModelOpt) or FP8 matrix as the repacks take it, through Core's matrix_parts and TensorReader. Other fusions are engine supplied.

agent_guidance.use_when: Weights are stored in a block-scaled low-precision format with a matching tensor-core MMA, and prompts of every length should use it without a second weight copy or per-call re-layout
agent_guidance.avoid_when: The device has no matching low-precision MMA, the engine can afford a second weight copy in a library's layout, or the format's scale grouping cannot be reconciled with the instruction's
provides: FP8 16x32 and NVFP4 16x64 tile repacking that moves bytes without re-encoding, plus NVFP4 scale tiles
FP8 W8A8 GEMM: a per-half k permutation turns each lane's tile bytes into its MMA fragment with byte permutes
NVFP4 W4A4 GEMM: lanes t and t^2 swap one word per register pair so each 16-value scale group sits in one lane pair
Activation packing in the matching slot order: per-token E4M3, or NVFP4 with the checkpoint's static input scale
Register-ring weight streaming, a 3-stage cp.async activation ring, two row tiles per warp and fixed-order split-K
Repacking each checkpoint tensor straight into its tile rows of a combined matrix: concatenated along N (q | k | v) or gate | up interleaved in 16-row tiles, FP8 row scales placed alike
Gated MLP prompt GEMMs writing BF16 act(gate) * up (SiLU, tanh-GELU, erf-GELU) from the accumulators or the split finish, with no FP32 [T][2I] output
Launch planning with scratch sizes and an fp4_mma_compiled() capability check; the default K split fills one wave of resident blocks (SM count x kernel occupancy) and never goes past it
A 1-16 row decode / verify GEMV over the same FP8 / NVFP4 tiles: exact BF16 decode in registers, mma.m16n8k16 BF16, each row's bits independent of M and of the other rows (plain and gated)
GEMV block shape from N, the SM count and the kernel's occupancy (the largest K split whose grid fits one wave), overridable to fix bits across devices

BF16-activation (W8A16 / W4A16) prompt GEMMs over the same tiles for checkpoints that cannot afford activation quantization: exact decode, BF16 MMA, FP32 fold every 512 columns, N % 16 and FP8 K % 32 tails handled, plain and gated
A device probe that measures the block-scaled MMA's scale-operand mapping and checks its value layout
A host model that proves the permutation, exchange and activation order with exact arithmetic
Checkpoint sources: one matrix's row-major codes and scales as zero-copy views, NVFP4 global and input scales as the kernels' divisors whatever the layout, FP8 scales one per row
engine_supplies: The stored tensors, repacked once at load before any reader
Scratch buffers sized from the plan for the largest prompt chunk
Plan parameters for its shapes and device (one GemvPlan per matrix shared by decode and verify), and fusion of activation quantization or other epilogues
Whole-model quality measurement of the W8A8 / W4A4 activation quantization
preserve: Every stored code and scale keeps its value; repacking only moves bytes
Activation slot order equals weight slot order, and scale groups stay inside one MMA scale group
A fixed accumulation order for a given launch shape, including the split-K finish
NVFP4 dequantization 1 / (weight_global_scale * input_global_scale) and the checkpoint's activation scale rule
Gate and up of a gated launch scaled exactly as the plain launch scales them; NVFP4 gate and up share the input global scale
One GEMV plan for decode and verify of a matrix: a row's bits depend only on the plan, not on M or the other rows
Exact BF16 decode of every stored value in the GEMV and the BF16-activation GEMM, and a bounded MMA chain before each FP32 fold
adapt: Tile shape and the permutation/exchange for another MMA instruction or format
Tokens per block, row tiles per warp, ring depth and the split threshold
GEMV group counts and ring depth; the BF16-activation GEMM's stage count, ring and fold length
Activation quantization fused into its producer instead of a separate packing pass

code_files.purpose: Tile layouts, plan, weight/scratch descriptors and launch interface
Repack, activation packing, FP8 and NVFP4 tensor-core GEMM and split-K finish kernels with launchers
BF16-activation kernels over the tiles: the 1-16 row decode / verify GEMV and the W8A16 / W4A16 prompt GEMMs, plain and gated, and their plans
Device helpers shared by the kernels: exact E4M3 / E2M1 decodes to BF16 fragments, BF16 MMA, tile loads, gated activation
Standalone device probe of the block-scaled NVFP4 MMA scale-operand mapping and value layout
Host model of tiles, register assembly and both MMAs with exact product checks
TileSource of a checkpoint matrix (NVFP4 compressed-tensors or ModelOpt, FP8 per tensor or row) through Core's matrix_parts and TensorReader

requires.hardware: CUDA C++17+; W8A8 prompt GEMMs need sm_89+, W4A4 prompt GEMMs an sm_120a or sm_121a build, the decode GEMV and the BF16-activation prompt GEMMs sm_80+; Python 3.11+ standard library for the host model
requires.model: Projection weights stored as FP8 E4M3 with per-row scales, or NVFP4 (E2M1 codes, E4M3 group-16 scales, FP32 global scale) with a static input global scale
requires.workload: Prompt GEMMs from one token to a full prefill chunk, sharing weights with a decode GEMV

contract.input: Row-major stored codes and scales (repacked once); BF16 activations [T][K]; plan, scratch and a CUDA stream
contract.output: FP32 [T][ldo] results written or added per element; tiles and scale tiles that a GEMV can share
contract.ownership: The engine owns weights, tiles, activations, outputs and scratch; launches borrow them until the stream reaches them
contract.failure: Unsupported shapes, non-positive sizes or global scales, and a plan made for another format, N or K or for fewer tokens return cudaErrorInvalidValue; the NVFP4 kernel traps where the block-scaled MMA is not compiled; launch errors are returned from cudaGetLastError
contract.core_boundary: No Core change; these are engine kernels inside its forward pass

dependencies: CUDA runtime with cuda_fp8.h and cuda_fp4.h
Python standard library for the host model and checkpoint sources (with crit_core)

validation.host: Exact host model: the FP8 permutation and the NVFP4 exchange reproduce direct dot products; wrong selectors or exchange partners do not; activation slots cover every column once
validation.native: CUDA test against an FP64 host reference with the same activation quantization for 1-300 tokens, split and unsplit, one or two row tiles per warp, add and fewer tokens than planned; a token's bits equal for every launch size a plan serves; repacking into place equals the fused matrix's repack byte for byte; gated launches within one BF16 ulp of act(gate) * up of the plain launch's rows for SiLU, tanh-GELU and erf-GELU, split and unsplit, and against FP64; plan mismatches refused; GEMV for M = 1-16 rows bitwise row invariant (and with rows reversed), deterministic, add exact, within 1.3e-7 of sum |wx| of FP64, every E4M3 code and E2M1 x E4M3 product decoded exactly, gated GEMV within one BF16 ulp of the plain rows, BF16-activation GEMMs against FP64 within 5e-7 of sum |wx| for 1-200 tokens and K up to 16384, split and unsplit, with row and K tails, token bits independent of T, add exact, gated within one BF16 ulp; GEMV and BF16-activation GEMM checks also through the software decodes of an sm_80 PTX build; fragment probe of the scale mapping and value layout on sm_120
validation.performance: One measured engine: 670 vs 550 TFLOPS (library GEMM with re-layout) on 17408x5120 NVFP4 matrices at 1,536 tokens on an sm_120 device; GEMV 1,420-1,700 GB/s (FP8) and 1,170-1,690 GB/s (NVFP4) for one row on an RTX 5090; BF16-activation GEMMs 155-205 TFLOPS from 512 tokens, 86-102% of cuBLAS BF16 on a dequantized copy; the one-wave default K split took 8% less time than a split to two blocks per SM over 40 prompt GEMMs there, within 5% of the best split in 35; no claim for other devices or shapes
